newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB bought no Tractebel stock in bid - Suez.
newsitem.headline: SGB bought no Tractebel stock in bid - Suez.

text.p: Shareholders of Belgian utility holding company Tractebel SA have not sold their shares to holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) in SGB's 14,500 franc per share bid for Tractebel, SGB parent company Compagnie de Suez said on Thursday.
"SGB did not have to buy a single Tractebel share," Suez chief executive officer Gerard Mestrallet told Belgian financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd in an interview.
SGB's bid for Tractebel closed on Wednesday.
In an effort to dissuade other shareholders from selling Tractebel stock to SGB, SGB had offered them a put warrant allowing to sell Tractebel stock to SGB at 14,500 francs in three years' time.

SGB made the public offer following its acquisition of a 25 percent stake in Tractebel from rival holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL) on September 17, an operation which boosted its Tractebel stake to 65 percent.
